statement: The function returns a result r such that len(r) = n and, for every i with 0 <= i < n, arrival[i] <= r[i]. For each integer t >= 0 define W_t = { i | 0 <= i < n, arrival[i] <= t, and r[i] >= t }. For each integer t >= 0 define d_t as follows: d_t = 1 if t = 0 or no i has r[i] = t-1; otherwise d_t = state[q] where q is the unique i with r[i] = t-1. For every integer t >= 0: (a) if W_t is empty, then no i has r[i] = t; (b) if W_t is nonempty, then exactly one i has r[i] = t, and if c is that person, then: if some j in W_t has state[j] = d_t, then state[c] = d_t and c <= j for every j in W_t with state[j] = d_t; if no j in W_t has state[j] = d_t, then c <= j for every j in W_t. These conditions determine r completely.
preconditions: Let n = len(arrival). n is an integer with 1 <= n <= 100000, len(arrival) = len(state) = n, arrival is non-decreasing (arrival[i] <= arrival[i+1] for 0 <= i < n-1), 0 <= arrival[i] <= n for every 0 <= i < n, and state[i] is either 0 or 1 for every 0 <= i < n. Here state[i] = 0 means person i wants to enter and state[i] = 1 means person i wants to exit.
